arStrings.szText:
Four men run through the dark tunnels of an ancient ruin, chased by demons. They come to a massive stone door. One of the men, a terrified Zakarum priest, deciphers the door's runes to find that blood is its key. He and two of the mercenaries spill their blood to open the way, leaving behind the last man to the demons.

The three men now stand in a cavernous chamber. Suddenly, their torches go out. One mercenary screams, wounded in the dark. The other swings at his attacker, only to find that it is the last man they left to die outside the door. He lets down his guise, now taking the form of a tall, pale man. By way of unseen magic, the two mercenaries hang in the air. The pale man speaks the beginning of an incantation. Coaxed to an eerie calm, the priest completes the incantation, his own body floating to hang mid-air. The men's blood wriggles from their bodies to form a thin membrane. A fist pushes from the other side of the membrane, then bursts through.

The horned demon Lilith, Daughter of Hatred, rebirthed in bloody sacrifice, comes to stand before the pale man. He kneels in respect, taking her hand as he welcomes her home.

"Blessed Mother... save us."
----
"Sanctuary was never meant for humankind. It was forged as a refuge from the war between the High Heavens and the Burning Hells. Instead, it became a new battleground in this Eternal Conflict. A secretive group called the Horadrim has kept mortals safe. But now this once-powerful order is a husk of what it was, and Sanctuary's ancient creators have returned to claim the hearts of humankind. This is the story of their downfall."

A lone Wanderer travels on horseback through a snowy landscape. One night, their horse bolts away in a fit of terror. The Wanderer searches, but only finds the horse's mauled, half-eaten corspe. Tired, cold, and now on foot, they seek refuge in a small cave. In their delirium, they see a vision of a wounded wolf, its skull bared and inscribed with runes. They scramble to their feet, afraid for their own sanity.

The blood petals reveal a vision from the past. At church, Nevesk's priest gives a passionate sermon, shaming his flock for their daily sins. But one voice challenges him. The priest sputters and the crowd watches in wonder as the demon Lilith gently descends upon the podium. Her form is terrifying, but she speaks softly, like a mother to her children. She warns of coming danger: the return of the Lords of Hell. If the people are to survive, it is not faith that will save them, but sin.

The priest cries out, ordering the crowd to resist her temptation--but a woman strikes him down before he can finish. Driven to a frenzy by Lilith's intoxicating presence, the townspeople gleefully beat him to a bloody death.

A pale, hooded man watches the violence from a distance. On her way out, Lilith orders him to continue their preparations in the Dry Steppes. "Now our true work begins."

The Wanderer searches the small cabin, but they are soon interrupted. The hermit who lives here has returned. Lorath Nahr stands in the doorway, carrying the carcass of a deer slung over his shoulder. "If you're going to trespass into my home, rifle through my things… then at least have the decency to join me for supper. I'm bloody hungry."

Donan yawns as he sits working at his desk late into the night. Suddenly, he is shocked into wakefulness by the appearance of a doorway in his chamber, covered by a curtain of flesh. Donan pulls it back to reveal none other than the demon Lilith. She stalks into his study, cornering him. He shakes in fear. "What do you want?"

Lilith is clear. "Astaroth." Donan insists that Astaroth is dead, but Lilith knows that Astaroth cannot die--at least, not by his hand. She leans in close to whisper in his ear. "You have grown so frail..." She caresses his lip, cuts it open on one claw. She offers to make him the hero he once was. Despite his terror, Donan is resolved to deny her. He shouts out. "Away, demon!"

Lilith and the doorway disappear in a fluttering cloud of blood petals. Donan stands alone in his study, left with only the dreamlike memory of her visit and the bleeding cut on his lip.

In an ancient chamber beneath Eldhaime keep, Lilith ponders Astaroth's soulstone. She offers him a deal: if he will give her safe passage to a place she is no longer welcome, then she will give him freedom... and more.

She turns to face Yorin, who cowers on the ground. "Donan's progeny. His pride and joy. Your retribution..." She grasps the boy by the neck and lifts him, pinning him against a wall.

Astaroth accepts her terms. Lilith smiles as she holds up the soulstone, brimming with energy. She plunges it into the front of Yorin's skull and he screams in agony. Searing heat radiates from the stone, charring his skin and filling his body with fire.

Donan rushes through the smoldering streets of besieged Cerrigar. He wails Yorin's name in search of his son. Blood petals float down from the sky. "He has been waiting for you." Lilith's voice answers him--she stands atop a ruined tower. Donan demands to know where Yorin is, and Lilith orders him to come forth.

A massive demonic beast with many toothed and snarling heads walks out from the smoke. Standing atop it is the fiery demon Astaroth, freed at last. The stone that kept him still juts out from his forehead. Astaroth taunts the man that imprisoned him for so long. "He called out for you... wept until his tears became fire." 

Donan falls to his knees, utterly broken. Lilith departs as the Wanderer approaches Astaroth, ready to fight.

The Knight Vigo stands guard at the Yelesna mines. A young girl, Neyrelle, argues energetically with him, demanding that he unbar the entrance to the mines. She claims to have seen a horned demon enter, and her own mother is trapped inside with it. Vigo is unmoved. His own Knights, trained professionals, are stationed in the tunnels. But Neyrelle is convinced that they are just as much in danger as her mother. Exasperated, she turns to the Wanderer for help.

The Wanderer strides into Inarius's chamber. The angel is massive, floating above the ground, his wings of light stretching out in tendrils to all corners of the room. His judgment is clear. "This is how you choose to approach me?" The Wanderer kneels in respect to ask him for his blessing, so they might cross the black lake and pursue Lilith. Inarius muses on his own struggle to end the Eternal Conflict and his banishment from Heaven. He lingers on the futility of Sanctuary and its mortals.

With fiery determination, the Wanderer stands. "I can stop her." But Inarius is unmoved. He dismisses them from his chamber.

Lilith stands over her son's corpse. She tenderly crosses hims arms over his chest as emotions come over her: first sorrow, then rage that his life, his future, was stolen from her. She doesn't know if he would've supported her vision for Sanctuary, but he was robbed of the choice all the same. She grasps the staff that impaled his chest and crushes it in her fist to reveal a key, hidden inside. The key to the gates of Hell. As she strides away, she makes a vow.

"Your sacrifice will not have been in vain."

An offering table lies at the center of a massive ritual chamber. The Tyrant King Brol patrols the area, and Lorath hides from his gaze in the shadows of a corner of the room. Elias stands over the table, which bears an unconscious woman. He lightly taps at a tattoo needle to etch ink into her skin--a ritual circle of some kind. A massive cloud of blood floats overhead. A masked cultist approaches and slits his own throat. Blood spills from his body, then floats to join the cloud above him. Elias reaches to swirl the tattoo needle's handle through the cloud, siphoning blood into its chamber.

But Lorath has seen enough. He runs out from his hiding place and grabs the needle. With no hesitation, he plunges it into Elias's throat. As Elias collapses, so too does the blood, which falls splattering all over the unconscious woman. She awakes with a blood-curdling scream. Lorath rushes the panicked woman from the room, leaving the Wanderer to face Brol alone.

A wounded monk scrabbles across the floor, panting and screaming in his frantic attempt to escape. But the wolves that chase him offer no mercy. They sink their fangs into his flesh and begin to eat him alive. Lilith and Elias stand nearby, observing, discussing the coming of the lords of Hell.

Elias believes that if they are to be saved, it will be by Lilith's hand. But she is clear that she did not come to Sanctuary to save--only to empower. "In my shadow, the strong will oppose the might of Hell itself. Let the weak fend for themselves."

Elias kneels before her. "Andariel lives. The Horadrim die. Whatever the cost."

At the desert chapel, the Wanderer grasps the Sightless Eye, peering into it to see a vision of Lilith and Elias. She contemplates the return of the Prime Evils, noting that her father's essence is reforming. She feels it, like a thousand old wounds ripping open again. Now, while he is vulnerable, is the best time to strike. Elias encourages her to make her father's power her own. But she holds up a hand to quiet him--something is amiss. Someone is watching... She looks directly into the Wanderer's gaze and pushes them out of the vision.

Lorath, Neyrelle, and the Wanderer stand before an altar bearing a bowl of lit incense. Purple smoke coils up and out from the flames, diffusing to fill the space. Neyrelle wonders what happens next, but Lorath only answers that they must wait for the path to appear.

Time passes. The trio are lulled to sleep by the smoke, sprawled out over various parts of the altar. Lorath shudders in and out of groaning wakefulness. He catches glimpses of something strange... a massive form, shifting, slithering.

Eventually, Neyrelle wakes him. "I think it worked."

Elias stumbles back, injured and bleeding. "How many times must we do this before you learn? My life is not yours to claim." The Wanderer knows different, though. They reveal that they've been to the depths of the Sunken Temple. They know Elias's secrets. Taissa quietly laughs nearby.

Elias looks at his severed pinky as the realization dawns that he is truly mortal again. He growls in frustration and casts a spell, disappearing into a cloud of smoke. Taissa sprints after him.

"I can sense your fear, father." Lilith stands before the gate to Hell, holding the key she took from Rathma's staff. The gates slowly swing open, bathing the Daughter of Hatred in glorious red light. She steps through.

The Wanderer peers into the Sightless Eye again. They see Lilith, still wounded, but standing tall as ever. She is meeting with Astaroth to collect on his debt. Astaroth questions her chances of victory, given her injury. But, cold and hard, she demands his compliance. Safe passage to the Cathedral of Hatred, in her father's domain of Hell: that was the deal. He bows his head in obedience, leaving to arrange it for her.

Lilith then senses the Wanderer's spying. She meets their gaze with fury in her eyes and her face fills their mind. She has caught them.

Donan lies on the ground, mortally wounded. Neyrelle, eyes red from crying, turns away to leave. She has watched enough of her loved ones die. Lorath wearily sits near Donan, who says he better not bury him here. But Lorath quips he's too damn old to haul his body out of Hell.

They speak of old men's regrets. Lorath says Donan should have turned to him instead of the Cathedral, that he would have shared Donan's burden. Donan says, "I know." He wonders how things may have been different, with Scosglen, and with Yorin. "Was it enough? Will he think it was enough?" His last breath leaves him. Only his corpse remains to hear Lorath's answer.

"Yes. More than enough."

Neyrelle grasps the soulstone. With determination, she plunges it into the orb of Mephisto's essence. She struggles to hold on as demonic energy ripples through the room. He gives her one final warning. "You have sealed your fate..."

The soulstone now glows blue with his essence. A portal out of Hell opens beside her--one last gift from the wolf. "Let us pray that worked. Come on." But the Wanderer cannot leave yet. "Lilith will hunt us down. I must end it." Neyrelle vows to find Lorath, and to wait for the Wanderer at the chapel. She turns to the portal, where the Herald waits beyond. "This better not be the last time I see you, understand?"

The Wanderer nods as she turns and leaves. After a brief moment, Lilith arrives at the Cathedral of Hatred, seconds too late. Furious, she prepares to destroy the Wanderer. "You will learn pain only glimpsed in myth."

Blood petals fall inside the Cathedral of Hatred. Lilith kneels, dying. She laments the futility of trying to escape the Eternal Conflict. "I gave you free will... and you've squandered it... wasting it on a crusade you don't understand..." Fury and hatred contort her features. "Without me... you would have no... victory. And its cost will be more... than you can pay."

First, Lilith's body turns to dust. Then, every blood petal that surrounds her follows, becoming grey and ashen. The Wanderer is left alone in the Cathedral that was once her home.

At Donan's grave in Scosglen, the Wanderer hands Lorath a letter from Neyrelle. "I spent a lot of time learning this code, so I hope you remember how to read it, Lorath. Because you are the last Horadrim now." Far, far, away, Neyrelle travels through an icy wasteland, soulstone in hand. She trips and falls, dropping the stone, before scrambling to snatch it back up. The wolf watches her.

"My mother would have wanted me to stay with you. She believed the Horadrim have all the answers. I don't know if she'd recognize this person I'm becoming. It's hard for me to think about her right now. But then I remember you and Donan. You weren't 'all-knowing Horadrim.' You were bitter. You were uncertain. But you were always true friends. That's what I hold onto because there is so much further to go." She sleeps on the floor in a corner of a dark warehouse, alone but for the wolf. She walks over dunes of sand, the heat of the sun beating down upon her. She sneaks onto the back of a traveling wagon under cover of night.

"Your imperfection gave me hope. And we will need it to face what comes next. To face him... and his brothers. I don't know how much time I have, but there has to be a better answer. And I have to find it. Alone. I know you'll want to go with me. But people have already died because I was not careful enough. I can't risk you too. If I've misjudged, the world is going to need you to survive and clean up the mistakes I leave behind." Lorath solemnly burns the letter in a brazier. He nods to the Wanderer before walking away, leaving them alone at Donan's grave.

"I know you don't want to hear this, but you don't get to quit. Not again. Wish me well, Lorath. Because if everything goes as I am hoping... We will never see each other again." Neyrelle pays for passage by boat. With soulstone in hand, she sails away over waters unknown.

At the Cathedral, Brother Iosef kneels before the Reverend Mother Prava, the leader of the church. She blesses him before turning to address the Wanderer. Iosef is dismayed to see them without Lorath, but the Wanderer explains he is busy with preparations to pursue Lilith. Prava had hoped for Lorath's help. But in his place, she asks the Wanderer to travel to Yelesna, where a demon sighting was reported. The details match the demon the Wanderer saw visions of in Nevesk.

The villagers of Nevesk offer their thanks to the Wanderer with ale and stew, celebrating and dancing into the evening. But something's not quite right… time slows down as the Wanderer sways and collapses, out cold. The food was drugged. The townsfolk watch in eerie silence as one villager loads the Wanderer's body onto a cart. As he wheels them out, we see the words of Rathma's prophecy overlaid on the scene:

"I saw my corpse,
and from my mouth crawled Hatred,
A father burned his children on a pyre,
and a mother molded a new age from the ashes,
I saw the weak made strong,
a pack of lambs feasting on wolves,
Tears of blood rained on a desert jewel,
and the way to Hell was torn asunder,
Then came a spear of light, piercing Hatred's heart,
And he who was bound in chains was set free.
-- Rathma's Prophecy"

In a blood-spattered, corpse-filled barn, the villager forces a bloody concoction into the Wanderer's mouth. Odd visions of a horned demon flash into their mind. Suddenly and silently, Iosef, a man of the cloth, sneaks in. Unhesitating, he swings his club into the villager's head, killing him instantly. He yells at the Wanderer to waken--the townsfolk are coming, and they must fight if they are to survive.

Over supper, the Wanderer recounts the strange visions they've had. Lorath surmises that the concoction the Nevesk villagers forcefed the Wanderer was actually the blood of Lilith. It forged a bond between Lilith and the Wanderer, and gave them the ability to see visions of her. But to be bonded to a demon is as dangerous as it is useful.

Lorath explains that Lilith is the Mother of Sanctuary and that it is prophesied that she would return, though her purpose is unclear. The Wanderer decides to find out what Lilith wants, first. Lorath offers them his aid and suggests they begin their search in Kyovashad. "If we can't stop Lilith, we'll all be damned."

Neyrelle finally finds her mother, Vhenard, kneeling at the center of a sprawling ritual circle filled with demonic runes. The circle was started in white chalk, but transitions to blood past a certain point--Vhenard must have run out of chalk. She is relieved to see Neyrelle, but her voice quavers. Something manic hides inside of her. She explains that she opened the way past this barrier for Lilith, but she could not follow after her. She lacks "the divine element." Neyrelle tries to get her mother to see sense, to stop writing in her own blood, but Vhenard explodes. Her love turns to vicious anger. She whips out a knife and accuses Neyrelle of trying to steal her work. She vows to finish the runes in Neyrelle's blood.

Neyrelle channels dark magic into her mother's corpse. Vhenard rises shakily to her feet, so glad to see her daughter again. Neyrelle is emotional, desperate to save her mother from death, but Vhenard knows her spirit must pass on. And Neyrelle must move on too.

Vhenard turns to the Wanderer. "You have the divine blessing. Your blood is the key." She jerkily stumbles to the ritual circle where the Wanderer spills their blood. Magic flows through her as she opens the way, revealing a bridge over the black lake. As she dies a second death, cradled in her weeping daughter's arms, she says a last goodbye.

"Neyrelle... you were so loved..."

The massive suit of armor collapses down to one knee. The Wanderer unlatches the torso plates, which slide open to reveal Vigo inside. His body is pierced all over by the armor's inner spikes. The Wanderer is alarmed, but Vigo is at peace. "This was a just punishment." He asks after Neyrelle and is glad to hear she is safe. With effort, he wrenches an impaled arms off of its spikes and holds out a charm to the Wanderer. This was Vhenard's bribe to him. He asks the Wanderer to pass it to Neyrelle. "I should never have taken it." The Wanderer comforts Vigo as he dies, paying the ultimate price for his sin.

Donan is engaged in a tense discussion with his son, Yorin, when the Wanderer arrives with a message from Lorath. Hearing that name shocks Donan. "Has the old man finally come down from the mountain?" The Wanderer explains that the demon Lilith has returned. Yorin pipes up, noting it might be related to what his father saw. Donan hesitates before admitting that there was an incident at his estate, though it would be best to meet and discuss it there.

Donan turns back to Yorin. "As for your request..." He allows Yorin to travel to the town of Braestaig, where Knights Penitent have been stationed. Yorin is overjoyed to get his father's permission, and swears to be safe in his travels.

The Wanderer meets Asgail, chieftain of Braestaig. "Donan sent me." Asgail scoffs. "At least you're not another Knight Penitent." A nearby Knight takes issue with her comment. He asserts that they're the ones protecting her village. Yorin steps in to dissipate the conflict. "Let it be." 

Asgail explains that a strange fog bearing mad spirits approaches Braestaig. But the Wanderer isn't here for that--they've come to ask after a demon that passed through. Asgail says the demon went uphill, to Airidah's domain, but that area is deadly. Yorin offers to take the Wanderer to Airidah himself. The Knight forbids this, concerned for the young man's safety. But Yorin insists he will be safe. "Donan puts his trust in this traveler. So shall we all."

Yorin examines ancient druid runes carved into the closed door. He haltingly translates some of them and discovers that a chant is required to open the way. Enemies approach. The Wanderer must fight them off while Yorin completes the chant.

Airidah sits on a cliff ledge, staring out into the fog. The Wanderer approaches to say that the people of Scosglen are dying at the hands of dead spirits. But Airidah is unbothered by this. "That is the way of nature." She believes the weak will be devoured, and the strong will rise to save Sanctuary from Hell. The Wanderer accuses her of believing Lilith's lies, yet Airidah is firm that this was her choice. "Lilith only granted me the power to do what must be done."

The Wanderer demands to know what Airidah gave Lilith in return. Of course, she won't offer this knowledge freely. Like everything in nature, it too must be earned. She invites the Wanderer to prove themself in combat.

The Wanderer returns to Nafain, who still hangs bisected and bleeding from a tree. He asks eagerly if the Wanderer stopped Lilith, but they answer no. She was already gone, and what's more, she left with a beast born from Nafain's own blood. He despairs at this news. He admits he told Lilith that Astaroth was hidden at Eldhaime, in exchange for the power to drive out the Knights Penitent from Scosglen. His fate, here on the tree, poisoning the very earth he called home, was not what he envisioned when he sought Lilith's aid. He asks the Wanderer for one final favor: death.

They grasp his spear and stab him. Nafain's wolf lets out a lonesome howl as he dies, at last.

The Wanderer returns to Eldhaime, where they find Donan gathering the bodies of slain Knights. The manor is in ruins after a recent attack by Lilith. She could've easily killed Donan, but she chose not to--he is convinced she's toying with him. Donan grunts in effort as he heaves the spear out of an impaled Knight corpse, pinned to the wall. He drags the body to lie beside the others as he admits the truth: he didn't vanquish Astaroth as all the stories claim, but instead he imprisoned the demon in a soulstone. Nobody knew this secret, not even his son. He built Eldhaime over the stone to contain its evil. That's where Lilith's gone: to the stone's chamber underneath the keep. 

But she hasn't won yet. Donan asks the Wanderer's help in stopping her. First, they must find Yorin.

Astaroth's defeated form lies prone on the ground. Donan falls to his knees beside it. He tenderly grasps the soulstone and pulls it from the demon's forehead. The massive body disintegrates into ashen cinders, revealing a small human corpse. Yorin.

Donan weeps. He cradles the boy to his chest, shaking and grieving. "I'm sorry, my son. I'm sorry..."

Inside the tent, a massive demon's corpse is held up against a large cross, its limbs tied down. Lorath approaches and notes that the demon was clearly Elias's work. "But where is he? The answer lies in the stomach."

He plunges a dagger into the demon's belly and cuts open a gash. He roots around in the wound and pulls out what he finds. A noble's severed hand. A lone boot. A medallion bearing the crest of the ruler of Guulrahn--now, the former ruler.

The barbarians protest at Lorath's crass treatment of these artifacts of the dead. They say the dead deserve respect.  "The dead deserve nothing when the living are in danger. Now, Guulrahn has a new ruler and we have Elias to thank for it." He turns to the Wanderer and asks them to meet him in Guulrahn.

Lorath stands at a cliff ledge that overlooks the ruined city of Guulrahn. The palace, where Elias has run to, lies in the distance, impenetrable. Zolaya, a woman who sits sharpening a blade nearby, interjects. She knows someone who can get them into the palace, through a secret tunnel. But this person, Oyuun, is missing, trapped in the city with the cannibals that overran it.

Lorath is skeptical--he's not even sure the tunnel exists, let alone if Oyuun still lives. Zolaya shakes her head bitterly. "You don't trust me." Lorath says of course not. She's a thief, and it's clear to him she has some other reason to seek out this Oyuun.

Zolaya scoffs as she turns away. "Not your business." But the Wanderer steps forward and asks where to look for Oyuun. Zolaya answers with hope that Oyuun had a house in the market. Lorath tells the Player to try to come back alive.

Oyuun stumbles forward, exhausted, into the open arms of Zolaya. Zolaya is overcome with tender emotion as the two embrace. Oyuun thanks her for waiting for her, despite the danger. "Oh, you stubborn cow, of course I waited! Where would I go without you to tell me?" She gently cups the other's face with her hands. Lorath watches from a short distance, a sniffle in his voice as he turns to the Wanderer. "You're a lucky fool, I'll give you that."  It isn't often he sees two lost souls reunited.

Zolaya explains to Oyuun that the Wanderer needs help getting into the palace. Oyuun tells what she knows: that there is an old escape tunnel with an entrance in the caves nearby, marked with the Overseer's Cross. She thanks the Wanderer as the two women climb atop a horse, before riding far, far away from Guulrahn and its horrors.

Lorath watches them go. "I think that was the merchant's horse. Best not to tell him."

In the eye of a whirling sandstorm, Elias stands before Taissa's unconscious, levitating body. He taunts the Wanderer for leading him straight to their camp due to their fumbling in the Sightless Eye. The Wanderer demands that he not hurt Taissa, but he only laughs. "Hurt her? I elevated her!" Taissa's blood-ink tattoos glow as Elias explains their purpose: they form a waypoint across realms. A large summoning circle appears on the ground, radiating red light, and Taissa's body floats over and drops onto its center. Neyrelle runs up to her and begins dragging her body away.

Elias isn't bothered. "It matters not. Her part is done. Your part is done too." He walks out into the roaring winds of the storm, leaving the Wanderer to face whatever horror will next come crawling out of his summoning circle.

The Wanderer peers into the Sightless Eye again. They see Lilith, still wounded, but standing tall as ever. She is meeting with Astaroth to collect on his debt. Astaroth questions her chances of victory, given her injury. But, cold and hard, she demands his compliance. Safe passage to the Cathedral of Hatred, in her father's domain of Hell: that was the deal. He bows his head in obedience, leaving to arrange it for her.

Lilith then senses the Wanderer's spying. She meets their gaze with fury in her eyes and her face fills their mind. She has caught them.
The Wanderer grasps the Sightless Eye. Mephisto speaks in their mind. "Take it and set yourself free."

Neyrelle grieves Donan's passing. "He gave everything. His home, his son. What was it for?" But she is interrupted by the appearance of a fiery portal. The Herald of Hatred stalks out from it, pleased to see the Wanderer still lives. Neyrelle is immediately suspicious. The Wanderer explains that the Herald helped them escape Lilith's trap. But Neyrelle recognizes the wolf for what it is... Mephisto. "You trusted a Prime Evil?"

The Herald speaks without emotion. "Trust had no part in it. Your friend saw reason instead. As should you. If Lilith takes my essence, Sanctuary is lost." Neyrelle hardens. She asks what he's proposing. But he has no proposals--he only offers his aid. The portal he came through leads straight to the Cathedral of Hatred, where his essence lies, reforming.

The Herald of Hatred approaches the Wanderer inside a cave that looks just like the cave they first met the wolf. He offers to free them from Lilith's trap. But they are skeptical--they ask why Mephisto keeps offering his aid. The wolf speaks plainly. "Look where we stand. I saved you in this dismal little cave because I sensed you could end Lilith. And that is all I want."

He says that one day, they will be enemies--but for now, they need each other to defeat Lilith. "Look me in the eye." The Wanderer falls to their knees, paralyzed by Mephisto's gaze. Demonic magic passes between the two. "The path ahead is steep. My blessing will guide you." The Herald walks away as the Wanderer shakily climbs back to their feet, now blessed by a Prime Evil.

In Hell, Lorath pushes for the group to use the Sightless Eye, as he believes it's the only way to find Lilith. Neyrelle is hesitant--she knows that the last time it was used, things didn't end well. While she and Lorath bicker, Donan wanders near a pillar made of corpses. But suddenly, one of the corpses snatches him and swipes at him. It wounds him deeply in his gut. He stumbles away, clutching his injury.

Back in the chapel, shaken, the Wanderer tells Lorath what they've seen of Lilith's plan to consume Mephisto's power. Lorath takes a moment to think. He has an idea for how to stop her, but they'll need the help of an old friend. He scribbles out a letter and passes it to the Wanderer. "Deliver this message to Donan. He'll have gone to Kyovashad for guidance."

"Donan and the Wanderer enter the vault's main chamber to find Neyrelle, hunched over a dusty tome. She startles at their arrival, scrambling up and wielding the Horadric Staff. ""Who is he?"" she asks the Wanderer. But Donan cuts in. ""'He' once lived in this vault. The one you're trespassing in. Explain yourself."" Neyrelle says she is a student researching the Horadrim. Donan is skeptical--he hopes that doesn't mean Lorath has taken her as another apprentice. But she clarifies that she is on her own. ""I don't need a teacher to study.""

Neyrelle emphasizes that Lilith is coming for Sanctuary, and she is doing all she can to prepare for that--with or without help. Donan doubts her ability to stand against Lilith, but decides to leave her be for now. He came to fetch something important from within the vault."

Meshif sits on the ground, badly hurt, as Lorath attempts to stop his bleeding. He greets the Wanderer gladly when they approach despite his wound. Lorath urges him not to talk, but he asks after Elias's fate anyway. With pain, he reaches behind his back to pull out a bottle of booze. He takes a hearty swig.

He offers the bottle to Lorath as he speaks. "Skewered like a quill rat. So it goes, eh Deckard?"

"Aye. So it goes." Lorath drinks in Meshif's honor as his body goes limp, dead at last. After a moment of silence, Lorath tells the Wanderer he's taking the Sightless Eye to study it, learn how to use it against Lilith and Elias. They'll meet at the desert chapel.

The Wanderer finds Lorath out cold, lying in a pile of mud. Unceremoniously, they dump a bucket of water over his head. He groans. They remind him that he asked them to meet him here. With slurred speech, he says he remembers--he's just surprised they're not dead. They ask what happened to him. "I was attacked, obviously. By vast quantities of alcohol, wielded by my own treacherous hand." 

The Wanderer cuts to the chase, and asks who the Pale Man is. Lorath is hesitant, but he admits that the Pale Man was once a Horadrim by the name of Elias. Moreover, he used to be Lorath's own apprentice. "He was the one who brought Lilith to Sanctuary." This revelation was what sent Lorath spiraling into his drunken bender.

Lorath wants to find him, figure out what else he's done, and ultimately, kill him. But first, he asks the Wanderer to find a woman who has some information for him.

The Wanderer stands over Iosef's corpse, conflicted. "He saved my life in Nevesk. They were not our enemies." Lorath grunts, exhausted. "They were fools... I don't have the time for it." He mounts a horse, which bears a cart carrying a wrapped corpse. He plans to bury Donan with his son in Scosglen.

The Wanderer quotes Lorath's own words back to him. "I thought the dead deserve nothing, while the living are in danger." Lorath chuckles. "Wise words. But I... I have a promise to keep." He goes on to say that's why the Wanderer must ride north ahead of him, to the Horadric Vault. If the Cathedral hasn't caught her yet, that's where Neyrelle will be. "Find her. Once you're together, meet me at Donan's estate." Lorath rides off.

Taissa, Donan, and the Wanderer sit in a small circle, sipping Taissa's brew. As time passes, the mind-altering tea takes hold, and senses become hazy. Taissa rolls on the ground; the Wanderer sits staring into empty space. Donan, though, becomes disoriented and paranoid. He hears his dead son's voice, even sees a vision of Yorin appear before him. Cut open by grief, he laments that he ever let Yorin leave Eldhaime in the first place.

"Why did you let me go?" Yorin asks. Donan quavers. "You were ready... you needed to go."

"I did. And I do again." The apparition of Yorin turns to walk away, but Donan falls to his knees, begging him to stay. Yorin walks away for the last time. Donan falls to pieces, sobbing through his pain.

Lorath and the Wanderer kneel over Neyrelle in concern as she writhes on the ground. "It burns! My arm..." Lorath explains that she's been infected by the Drowned. He rushes to start a fire from driftwood and thrusts the blade of his polearm into the flame. "I must remove the Drowned necrosis!" Neyrelle is confused. The Wanderer cuts in. "Lorath, are you certain?" Lorath says he's certain she's dying. He ties a tourniquet on her arm. He fetches his polearm, its blade now red-hot from the fire. She whimpers in agony, clutching her arm, but Lorath pushes. "We have no choice. Hold her!"

The Wanderer wrenches her arm out and pins it down. Lorath aims his blade at her elbow. He pulls back, and swings down overhead with effort. Neyrelle screams in agony and passes out.

Lorath gently bandages her stump. "You will be Horadrim, young one. I will not fail you."

Elias, defeated at last, lies prone on the ground. Taissa hovers over him, but Lorath interjects--he must speak with Elias before she kills him. A crow perches on a nearby branch, watching their exchange, waiting. Lorath speaks to Elias like a father to a lost son. "Oh, Elias. Was all this worth it, then?" But Elias has no regrets for his deeds. He's proud of bringing Lilith to Sanctuary, of preparing to fight against the coming Lords of Hell. Something Lorath dared not try. "'Was it worth it?' That is a coward's question, Lorath. It suits you."

Lorath wrenches away, done. Taissa steps in and slits his throat. "The Tree does not forgive debts." She cups his face as he dies, gurgling, choking on his own blood. The crow swoops down and viciously pecks at his neck, severing his head.

Inside his workshop, Donan takes several deep breaths, readying himself to mend the stone. He jumps into action. "Mallet," he demands. The Wanderer passes him the tool. Donan speaks the Horadric tongue as he begins striking the stone, ethereal sparks flying from each impact. "Sulfur," he asks next. His striking grows to a frenzy as he yells out the Horadric chant. At last, with a final swing of the hammer, the stone emits a powerful pulse of light. It is whole again. 

Taissa is amused. "Was it so easy, then?" Donan pushes back, saying she has no idea the toll such a task of magic takes. The Wanderer cuts in to dissipate the tension. Their next goal is clear: they must return with the stone to Zakarum keep.

The Wanderer approaches an open coffin that leans upright against a carved stone statue. They hear the whispers of the Tree. "Fear not this cradle... Colder beds than this await you yet, traveler..." They step into the coffin and the lid closes shut over them.

The coffin slides into the water. The Wanderer breathes heavily, faster and faster, as the coffin begins to bob. Their breaths turn to struggling gurgles, then quiet drowning, as the coffin slides under the surface. The Tree whispers a final message. "His debt must be paid."

Lorath, Neyrelle, and the Wanderer approach the Tree of Whispers. Severed heads hang from the tree's branches. Suddenly, they all turn to face the trio. Many rotting mouths speak in a disjointed chorus. "Why have you come?" Lorath answers that they seek a man, Elias. The heads hiss. They explain that the Tree deals in thoughts: it offers an insight, in exchange for a head. It seems Elias is the first to escape payment. Neyrelle asks what insight the Tree gave him.

A head answers that he sought the way to summon Lilith, but made a stop on his journey to a place beyond the Tree's sight. Lorath intuits that stop is why Elias has been impossible to kill, up til now. Another head rasps that that is why Taissa failed to deliver his head. The Tree points the trio to a coffin beyond the wrecks. "Find out what secrets linger there, for the Tree knows not."

Prava, ringed by Knights, opens her arms to welcome Donan and the Horadrim. "The Father will deliver us, together." But Donan angrily points out that Inarius seized their soulstone. To Prava, this was only the will of the Light. "How can you doubt us after everything we've done for you and Yorin? At least he doesn't have to see you like this."

Her insult, delivered with his son's name in her mouth, enrages Donan. He moves to attack her, but Lorath jumps in to hold him back. The Knights draw their spears, stopped only by Prava's order to stand down. She steps in closer. "Sin reaps consequence. I have faith the Father acted righteously." For once, Lorath is the peace maker. He points out that they share a goal: to stop Lilith. Prava rallies the troops to meet Inarius at the gate to Hell.

Inarius's voice echoes over the city as the Horadrim step through the gate. A battalion of Knights listens in rapt attenion as he vows to slay Lilith, as decreed by propechy. He orders the troops to rally at the palace. Today, they march on Hell. "And after that? Your plan?" Lorath boldly questions the angel. Inarius is unmoved. He makes it clear the angels have no need of the Horadrim. But Lorath pushes. He asks Donan to brandish the stone. "We don't need the bloody angels either."

The stone wobbles in Donan's grasp, before springing to Inarius's hand, pulled telepathically. "The hubris." The angel criticizes them for boasting of a mere fragment of what was once the worldstone. He floats upwards and away, leaving the Horadrim without a stone or a plan.

In Hell, Prava leads legions of Knights to battle. She steps barefoot through the fires, her feet charred, preaching in Inarius's name. The angel himself joins his armies, his light spreading to illuminate the masses of demons that await them. Prava kneels and bows in a show of utter faith as Hell's legions rush to meet her. Miraculously, she is kept safe by her Knights' spears and shields.

Inarius catches sight of Lilith and leaves to chase her on his own. She confronts him away from the fight. She asks what it is he's truly after. He is adamant that his place is in the Heavens. But she is skeptical. "Is that why you seek to destroy all that we created?" Inarius roars that Sanctuary is an abomination. But Lilith presses harder. "And our son?" Inarius confesses his deed, that he killed Rathma to satisfy the heavens. Lilith speaks quietly. "Tell me... did they rejoice? No? They do not want you." Inarius, enraged, stabs Lilith through the gut.

He turns away now, yelling out to the unhearing Heavens, demanding to know what he must to do ascend once more. Lilith stabs him in the back. He screams, begging for Heaven's protection as she pins him down and rips his wings from his back. She stalks away, leaving behind his smoldering corpse.

Outside, the battle still rages. But without Inarius's protection, Prava and her Knights begin to falter against the swarming legions of Hell.

At the desert chapel, the Wanderer grasps the Sightless Eye, peering into it to see a vision of Lilith and Elias. She contemplates the return of the Prime Evils, noting that her father's essence is reforming. She feels it, like a thousand old wounds ripping open again. Now, while he is vulnerable, is the best time to strike. Elias encourages her to make her father's power her own. But she holds up a hand to quiet him--something is amiss. Someone is watching... She looks directly into the Wanderer's gaze and pushes them out of the vision.
